body: Homeostasis describes regulated conditions in the body, such as temperature, staying within ranges compatible with function. When body temperature rises, evaporation of sweat can remove heat. This is a feedback process because the response changes the condition that helped trigger it.

Several systems help protect tissue from damage and infection. Skin and other barriers restrict entry. Immune cells can respond to signs of damage or foreign material; some mount more targeted responses. Antibodies can bind specific targets, and some immune cells persist after a response, supporting a faster response on later encounters.

limitations: Normal ranges and responses vary across people and circumstances. These examples describe basic physiology, and immune activity can also damage healthy tissue.
purpose: Distinguish regulation of internal conditions from responses to threats.
